texts: How we rig a 3D garment: put it on a body, rig the pair, then take the body away

A shirt has no skeleton, so our garment forge rigs each piece while a reference body is wearing it, then removes the body and keeps the weights the cloth picked up from the joints underneath. The write-up covers the seven stages, the gates a piece has to pass, and what binding to a skeleton does not fix yet: three.ws/wardrobe

issues.problem: Mechanical check flags "actually" as filler in the article body; the sentence carries the fact without it.
issues.fix: Change to "from the arm bones it sits on". Same for "bones a body really has" ("bones a body has") and "very different proportions" (state the tolerance or say "different proportions").

issues.problem: The cover alt text and body caption present static renders as garments "turned in its live 3D viewer"; the stills cannot show interactivity, and the cover image shows three renders on a dark background with no viewer chrome. This is defensible but the wording slightly overstates what a still depicts.
issues.fix: In the cover alt text, drop "in their live viewers" or recapture with the visible viewer UI (3D button or orbit controls) so the image supports the caption.
